In order for GladModel to identify which arrays that should be couples
from the two chip types, they have to have the same 'name' (as defined
by aroma.affymetrix; see online docs). They can still have different
'tags'.

From the above you can see that GladModel thinks there are 60 unique
samples and 30 were hybridized to one chip type and 30 to the other.
I guess this is not what you want. If it the case that the first 6
digits specifies the sample, you have to rename your fullnames
"1120013" and ""1120014" to have fullnames "112001,3" and "112001,4",
and so on. That way they get the same names ("112001") and only
differ in tags ("3" and "4").

You can indeed rename your files manually in order to avoid having to
refit everything, but you have to be careful to get it right. I also
strongly recommend that you rename all your files in rawData/,
probeData/, and plmData/ accordingly; if you do that you should be
able to use the identical script you used now and aroma.affymetrix
will recognize already done work.

Please make sure to read about filename, names, tags, fullnames etc
online; it is very important and extremely useful to understand how
that works.

That seems to be a bug, because it should have returned a 60x2 array
with the same first column, but the array indices in the 2nd column
should be in rows 31:60. I'll put it on the todo list to fix.

As explained above, this bug is not the cause of your problem but the
reason for the error message you get.

Cheers

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: question about an error displayed after fit(glad)
parts:
A quick follow up on this: I have located the bug in
getTableOfArrays() causing the segmentation model to give an error on
invalid indices. Note, you still have to solve the cause of the
problem of naming you files according to the <name>,<tags> format in
order for aroma.affymetrix to be able to pair up hybridizations from
different chip types. In other words, with the bug fix but still with
the incorrect filenames, you would no longer get an error, but instead
aroma.affymetrix would infer that you have used 30+30 arrays where
half is for one chip type and the other half on the other. This would
result in 60 segmented "samples". So, make sure to get your filenames
right.

/Henrik

I have committed a patch that fixes the above. To install the patch, do:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: question about an error displayed after fit(glad)
parts:
Forgot to say, until next release, the bug fix can be installed as a patch:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

/Henrik

On Mon, Mar 31, 2008 at 1:32 PM, Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> A quick follow up on this: I have located the bug in
> getTableOfArrays() causing the segmentation model to give an error on
> invalid indices. Note, you still have to solve the cause of the
> problem of naming you files according to the <name>,<tags> format in
> order for aroma.affymetrix to be able to pair up hybridizations from
> different chip types. In other words, with the bug fix but still with
> the incorrect filenames, you would no longer get an error, but instead
> aroma.affymetrix would infer that you have used 30+30 arrays where
> half is for one chip type and the other half on the other. This would
> result in 60 segmented "samples". So, make sure to get your filenames
> right.
>
> /Henrik
>
> I have committed a patch that fixes the above. To install the patch, do:
>
> library(aroma.affymetrix);
> downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");
>
>
>
>
